### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via installActivityReadVisibility (symbol, a top-level function), installAuditLogReadVisibility (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via hasObjectMiddleware (literal, a string literal on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9810dd9d1a29848b3ae848152d8ac84ccb9557f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ae977afb7b121c292d7225b7982bcc0c997678fc` — the merge of head `3ecca941d6c4aa571cf213bf757449b02b3c8e11` into base `c9810dd9d1a29848b3ae848152d8ac84ccb9557f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ae977afb7b121c292d7225b7982bcc0c997678fc && git checkout ae977afb7b121c292d7225b7982bcc0c997678fc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c9810dd9d1a29848b3ae848152d8ac84ccb9557f 3ecca941d6c4aa571cf213bf757449b02b3c8e11 && git checkout -B drift-repro c9810dd9d1a29848b3ae848152d8ac84ccb9557f && git merge --no-ff 3ecca941d6c4aa571cf213bf757449b02b3c8e11

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9810dd9d1a29848b3ae848152d8ac84ccb9557f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c9810dd9d1a29848b3ae848152d8ac84ccb9557f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3ecca941d6c4aa571cf213bf757449b02b3c8e11`
Local-runs: none

PR #23693 for card #23673 (ADR-0139 row E5), read at 2026-10-15T16:07Z. Inputs: the card's body and its five comments (triage 6192519330, the claim 6192750084, the owner's precondition reading 6192900751, the dev report 6196293752, the question to the owner 6196364237); the PR's body, its 11-file list and its net diff against `main` at the merge base `c24598658d`; the 41 check-runs on the head; ADR-0139 (D2 to D5, the consumer table, Consequences, the plan's row E5) and ADR-0112; #22788 with its six comments (notes 1 to 3, pointers 6107554336, 6113122770, 6115710018); PR #23663 (`94924e01c1`, the `canReadObject` admission this gate builds on); and, on `origin/main`, the engine's composition seam (`ObjectQL#refuseUncomposableReadableIdsClasses`, `#readableIdsScopeOf`, `#resolveDatasourceBinding`, `#resolveEffectiveDatasource`, `#hasObjectMiddleware`), `audit-writers.ts#AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS`, `activity-field-redaction.ts#computeWithheldUpdateFilter` and its middleware, `security-plugin.ts#canReadObject` and `#getReadFilter`, `auth-event-audit.ts`, `filter-comparand-shape.ts#readableIdsRefusalError`. Nothing built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on the head, as read:** 41, all completed. 35 success, 6 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in, Temporal Conformance main-only), 0 failure. The required set is success: Lint and Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core and its six shards, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard. Also success: Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness, the four Type Check jobs, the three card-and-branch claim checks. No governed path in the file list.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public surface: none moves — right.** `src/index.ts` at the head re-exports nothing from `parent-record-read-gate.ts`, `activity-read-visibility.ts` or `audit-log-read-visibility.ts` (only `comment-access-hooks.js` symbols among these modules). The installers' engine parameter widens from `CommentAccessEngine` to `ParentRecordGateEngine`, an intersection whose added members (`registry`, `hasObjectMiddleware`, `resolveEffectiveDatasource`) are all optional, so every prior argument is still accepted; and the installers are not exported anyway. The two REST reads declare no new query parameter.

**The access floor, path by path — no path serves a row the caller may not read. Right.**
- *The leaf class.* `computeParentRecordFilter` writes `{ object_name: P, record_id: { $in: ReadableIds.of(P) } }` for every registry object outside `AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS` and outside the gated object, and makes no engine call for it. The engine composes each leaf at its executor boundary from `canReadObject(P, caller)` and `getReadFilter(P, caller)` and answers `$in: []` on a refusal, a throw, the deny sentinel, an absent service or a parent the registry does not hold (`readableIdsScopeOf`). A leaf is therefore never wider than a direct read of P except for D5's second class, which the gate routes to the probe by the very function the engine refuses on (`hasObjectMiddleware`).
- *The outside-class predicate* (`ledgerRowAboutNoRecordWhere`): `record_id` null or empty, a non-null action, and the action not in `LEDGER_RECORD_ACTIONS` — the same set `isLedgerRowAboutNoRecord` reads, and the same three tests in the same order (that function already refuses any row carrying a record id before it looks at the action). Equal to the in-process form, so the served set for this class is main's. The existing `audit-log-read-visibility.integration.test.ts` (untouched, green on this head) drives it end to end with `record_id: null` rows for `config_change`, `import`, `platform_admin_standing_change`, and a `record_id: null` `update` row that must stay excluded.
- *The no-`canReadObject` branch* (`planParentReads` returns `no-object-admission`): the whole read goes to the probe, where `admittedParentObjects` answers `null` and every parent is read as the caller through the middleware — exactly main's behaviour in that state, and said once.
- *The exemption* (`view_all_audit_log`): decided at step 0 of `computeParentRecordFilter`, before anything is enumerated; nothing written for the holder. Unchanged.
- *A parent bound to another datasource.* The gate compares `resolveEffectiveDatasource` (which answers `undefined` for a `via: 'default'` binding) where the engine compares `resolveDatasourceBinding().datasource` (which answers the default driver's natural name for the same binding). The only disagreement is a parent explicitly bound to the default driver's own name: the gate probes it where the engine would compose. Stricter, never looser, so no composition refusal can reach the consumer from a mis-classified parent, and the probe it lands on is bounded and fail-closed. On a telemetry-split deployment every parent of the ledger is probed, the limit D5.3 records.
- *The `sys_session` parent* (`LEDGER_NAMED_PARENTS`): no object-scoped middleware is registered for `sys_session` on main, so it is a leaf, composed from `canReadObject('sys_session', caller)` and `getReadFilter('sys_session', caller)` — the `sys_session_self` RLS policy — the same two halves the middleware applied to the probe's caller-scoped read of it on main. Served set equal to main's.
- *A delegated caller*: the whole read is the probe, decided by the engine's own test (`onBehalfOf.userId`).
- *The gated object itself and the sibling stream*: excluded from enumeration by name; `sys_activity` and `sys_audit_log` are both in `AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS`, so neither is ever a leaf of the other.
- *The withheld-update rule's SYSTEM re-read* (consumer 3): its pre-scan composes this gate's leaves for the system (`canReadObject` answers `true` and `getReadFilter` answers `undefined` for `isSystem`), so its window is the first 2,000 rows of the whole stream in the caller's order; its `id $in` or `$nin` is then ANDed with the reader's own leaves, which the executor boundary composes for the reader on the outer read. Narrowing only.

**Served-set changes, each named — right.** (a) The ledger: a non-holder's broad read is served every row about a record it may read and every outside-class row, with a true `total`, on any table size — a widening *within* the caller's read; the window was the defect. (b) The activity stream: the gate has no window, but the stream stays capped by consumer 3's window (measured: member 725 of 1,816, administrator `total` 1,999) — not widened past access, and not the card's pin either (③). (c) The old "no candidate, nothing to narrow" shortcut (`if (!candidates.length) return null` at the base) is gone: a read the probe finds no row for is now narrowed to deny-all (the stream) or to the outside predicate (the ledger) — narrowing only, pinned. (d) On `driver-mongodb` both reads now fail `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 — ADR-0139 D3 and Consequences, note 3 on #22788.

**D3 — right for the two gates this card names.** Neither consumer wraps `computeParentRecordFilter` or `next()` in a catch any more. The gate's own remaining catch is around `probeBranches` alone: a fault of the probe (its SYSTEM pre-scan, `canReadObject`, `resolveReadableParentIds`) answers deny-all and is said — that pre-scan carries no leaf (the gate has not ANDed yet), so it cannot meet a composition refusal. The envelope a caller gets: `readableIdsRefusalError` sets `code: INTERNAL_ERROR`, `status: 500`, `httpStatus: 500`; under ADR-0112's 5xx amendment an author-declared server fault keeps its message, so the driver, the leaf and the remedy survive to the door. The new integration suite pins `{ code, status }` and the driver's name in the message for a refusing driver on both objects, `find` and `count`. Consumer 3's middleware (`activity-field-redaction.ts`, lines 562 to 572 on main) still catches its pre-scan failure into `WITHHELD_DENY_ALL`; on a refusing driver that pre-scan is the one refused, so it logs "pre-scan failed, denying all" while the leaves stay in the outer WHERE and the caller still gets the 500. That consumer is E6's row by the ADR's table; the card names "these two gates". Carried to E6 as the dev routed it — not a defect of this diff.

**D5 — the probe path for the three classes is main's.** `probeBranches` is the base's steps 1 to 3 with a `restrictTo` added: the same SYSTEM pre-scan at `PARENT_GATE_SCAN_LIMIT` in the caller's order, `canReadObject` first, then one caller-scoped read per admitted parent, the same cap warning now naming the class. For classes 2 and 3 the window holds only rows naming those parents. Chosen up front in `planParentReads`, never by catching.

**The no-`canReadObject` guard (the dev's found-and-closed interplay) — sound.** Without `canReadObject` the engine admits a leaf by `explain`, which refuses a SYSTEM context, so consumer 3's SYSTEM pre-scan would see no row of any parent and serve the update rows it never judged. Routing the whole read to the probe in that state puts literal id lists in the WHERE, which mean the same under every context, and equals main's behaviour exactly. Its bound: the guard keys on the method's presence, not on its SYSTEM answer; plugin-security's `canReadObject` admits `isSystem` by source, and no in-tree service answers otherwise. A third-party service whose `canReadObject` refused SYSTEM would reopen it — carried in the dev's second out-of-scope finding to #22788 (engine lane), and a right carrier.

**Pins read against the diff:** the leaf integration suite (14 cases on a real engine and SQL driver: past the window with a true total, no unreadable or vanished parent served, no caller-scoped read of a leaf parent, one leaf per enumerated parent beside the probed classes, the delegated probe, the ledger whole, the predicate, the holder, the branch-count reading for note 1, and the refusing driver); the unit files (the five probe states, D3's two no-catch cases, the exemption before enumeration, the named session parent, the predicate's shape); the withheld integration case with `canReadObject` withdrawn; #23663's admission suite re-pointed to tell the probe's questions from the engine's; the dogfood ledger pin past the old window newest-first. Each is named with its ablation in the PR body; the check-runs on the head are the verdict on them.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23673-parent-gate-readable-ids.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-audit` `minor`. Matches what a consumer observes: more rows served within access and a true `total` (a fix), no exported declaration added, removed or narrowed, no accept-set change on either route, and one new failure mode on a refusing driver — a ruled consequence (ADR-0139 D3, Consequences; #22788 note 3) that E3 and E4 already shipped on `driver-mongodb` at `minor` (`.changeset/23639-readable-ids-drivers.md`). The changeset names both the mongodb 500 and the activity cap that remains until E6, so it advertises nothing the runtime does not deliver.

Clause-②: no — no published declaration moves; the modules the diff rewrites are not re-exported, and no input is newly accepted.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Q1 (is `sys_session` a ledger parent; D4's enumeration vs "excluded exactly as today") — answered: reading A, and it widens nothing.** D4's parenthetical says the enumeration's exclusions are the rows the probe already excluded, "exactly as today". `sys_session` is in the CRUD mirror's `SKIP_OBJECTS`, but the ledger's auth-event sink writes `object_name: 'sys_session'` rows (`auth-event-audit.ts`), and on main the probe judges them by a caller-scoped read of `sys_session` under `sys_session_self`. Reading B would newly exclude a member's login rows about its own live session — a narrowing no ruling asked for and contrary to D4's own invariant. Reading A keeps the served set equal to main's through the mechanism D4 names, declared per writer in one constant. The activity stream's one producer is the mirror, so for it the literal enumeration is exact. The owner's confirming nod (asked at 6196364237) is appropriate; this record finds no access change either way.
- **Q2 (land E5 with the card's activity pins carried to E6) — escalated; this is the landing condition.** The card's done line carries three activity pins: the plan row's "1,808 of 1,808", and the director's two (6115710018: an administrator's `total` of 4,201 not 2,000; a member sees every row past the old window). Measured on a real stack they are not met (725 of 1,816; 1,999). The ADR's own text already places their last bound in E6: its consumer table, row 3, says the withheld-update rule "sits on consumer 1's read path, so its bound caps the read even once consumer 1 is pushed down", and D4 makes that rule a predicate in E6, after E5 — the plan row's E5 pin and its row 3 disagree, and the director carried the pins to "E5 / E6" together. So the diff is right and the card's pins are the owner's to move. ⛔ Until `domain:engine` seat 1 answers Q2 by moving the two activity pins to E6's set on #22788 and amending #23673's body, the PR must not land with `Fixes #23673`: that would close a card against a done line the runtime does not meet. If the owner holds E5 instead, the PR waits. If the owner moves the pins, the PR lands as is. (Rewording to `Part of` changes the two card-and-branch check-runs' reading, so the keyword is settled by the owner's answer, not by this record.) The seat decides; this record's PASS is a verdict on the diff's contract, not a licence to close the card as it is written today.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1** (consumer 3's SYSTEM window still caps `sys_activity`; its catch logs "denying all" on a refusing driver while the read still fails 500) — carrier E6 on #22788, agreed; read in source above.
- **Out-of-scope finding 2** (`explain` refuses a SYSTEM context where `canReadObject` admits it, so a leaf composed under SYSTEM selects everything or nothing by which half the service offers) — carrier #22788 engine lane, agreed; it is also the bound of this PR's guard, named above.
- **Out-of-scope finding 3** (the engine composes each leaf with the outer read's full envelope, operation-private keys included) — carrier #22788, agreed; no wrong answer measured, and plugin-security re-stamps `__readScope` per object.
- **Out-of-scope finding 4** (`driver-mongodb`: both streams' reads 500, the Console's header bell and Home activity card error on such a deployment) — O3, a ruled consequence; the changeset says it.
- **Interim letter C**: never landed (ruling W on #22889), so the card's "retire it" line had nothing to retire; the PR says so. Right.
- **The dev's deviations** (three tsc reads outside the verify lock, a dts-closure re-run after a concurrent build, the merge commit amended for the model-free trailer pair before its first push, one A0 leg re-run after a commit, scratch dogfood files absent from every commit, the gate list re-derived on the branch) — none touches the diff's contract or its pins.
- **One note, no action owed:** the gate's docblock says the predicate is "pinned row for row against a real driver in `audit-log-read-visibility.integration.test.ts`". That suite exists on main and the PR does not touch it; its fixture rows do exercise the predicate end to end through the real gate on this head, so the claim holds as a reading, but no case was added for the predicate's new form beyond the unit shape test.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23673-parent-gate-readable-ids`
Reviewed-by: `session_017WLmd5in9RXu7AjyHR8fKQ`

**VERDICT: PASS**

**Verdict: ACCEPT of the diff at head `3ecca941d6c4aa571cf213bf757449b02b3c8e11`, with the landing HELD on the card owner's answer to Q2.** The contract-tier record `6196593905` (`Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, **VERDICT: PASS**) is on this head, and it escalates Q2 as the landing condition.
